A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GroundingME and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Corresponding methods, tables, figures, and relocated appendix sections support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 25 MLLMs, test-time selection and fine-tuning experiments, human rejection verification, and tool-use results.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds a reasoning-aware multimodal judge result, annotator-agreement measurements, and prompt-robustness results.

M1.justification: Section 5.2 extends reasoning-based selection to a multimodal Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-Thinking judge receiving candidate reasoning trajectories. V1 used text-only judges for trajectory assessment and multimodal judges for final-answer assessment. The pairwise best-of-16 procedure, benchmark construction, and data-mixture training remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 1,005-example GroundingME benchmark, four dimensions and twelve subtasks, SA-1B and HR-Bench image sources, and positive/negative RefCOCOg training and evaluation data. Ref-Adv is added only to the related-benchmark comparison, not actually evaluated.

E2.justification: Table 4 expands the evaluated judging alternatives with Qwen3-VL-A22B using candidate reasoning trajectories. Both text-only judges and both answer-only multimodal configurations remain. This adds a comparison configuration, while the main 25-model evaluation roster is unchanged.

E3.justification: V2 adds a same-model comparison with and without candidate reasoning, evaluations using five distinct prompts for two models, and an agreement assessment on 50 randomly sampled examples. Existing benchmark metrics, decoding settings, best-of-16 sampling budget, and fine-tuning protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a reasoning-access ablation, prompt-sensitivity and output-format checks, and inter-annotator validation. Appendix B further examines subtask ranking differences and the Small subtask's contribution to scaling anomalies using existing Table 3 results. Earlier thinking, data-mixture, human-verification, and tool-use analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports accuracy with ± values across five prompts and pairwise Cohen's kappa for annotator agreement. The meaning of ± is unspecified, and neither version provides seed-based uncertainty for the main benchmark results. These additions do not establish increased repeated-run counts for existing experiments.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds the multimodal-with-reasoning result: 54.3 overall, with 66.7/79.7/46.3/15.9 across the four categories; existing rows remain unchanged. New results include kappa 0.64–0.73 (mean 0.69), prompt accuracies 31.36±2.02 and 10.07±0.44, and 98.61% format compliance. The main benchmark and fine-tuning scores are retained.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. Task definitions and the IoU-based accuracy and mAcc definitions remain unchanged. The added empirical agreement statistic does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract raises the reported maximum test-time selection gain from 2.9 to 4.5 percentage points, reflecting the added judge configuration. The introduction now claims improvements across all subtasks. The central benchmark and grounding-gap claims remain, while explicit safety language and the conclusion's prescriptive claims are softened.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 shifts emphasis from judges' inherent multimodal ability to the benefit of accessing reasoning trajectories. Appendix B adds possible OCR and training-data explanations for ranking differences and attributes Limited-category scaling irregularities to Small objects. The existing limitation concerning fine-tuning's cost to positive out-of-domain grounding is retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly discloses rule-based recovery of malformed responses, without specifying the rules. Existing prompt templates, training details, and project link remain unchanged. The five alternative prompts and a dedicated template for the new multimodal-with-reasoning configuration are not supplied.

R1.justification: V2 adds Ref-Adv to Table 1 and related-work citations, and cites VL-RewardBench, Multi-Crit, LLaVA-Critic, and PhyCritic when positioning judge-based selection. Four application-oriented autonomous-driving and human–robot-interaction references are removed. The benchmark's overall novelty positioning remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 edits and shortens the abstract, introduction, and conclusion, rewrites Section 5.2 around thinking quality, and adds acknowledgments. The appendices gain cross-dimensional and prompt-robustness subsections, with existing material renumbered and relocated. Most prose and the main section structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 7–8 visualizing existing Table 3 results, regroups Table 4 by reasoning access and adds a row, and adds Ref-Adv to Table 1. Figure 1's caption is clarified, appendix material is repositioned, and example images use higher resolution. Existing examples and principal figures remain.

improvement.justification: V2 modestly strengthens validation through annotator agreement and prompt-sensitivity checks, and the same-model reasoning-access comparison in Table 4 better supports the test-time selection argument. The additional subtask analyses improve diagnosis without changing the benchmark's scope. Missing prompt variants, recovery rules, and a definition of the ± statistic limit reproducibility, but the added evidence provides a clear, bounded overall improvement.
